research_question: In adults undergoing surgical management of ankle (or lower limb) fractures, what is the effect of postoperative immobilisation with a removable ankle support (e.g. removable brace, orthosis, walking boot, functional support) compared with a non-removable support (e.g. plaster cast or other non-removable immobilisation) on activity limitation / ankle function at the end of the treatment period?
treatment_label: Removable ankle support (removable brace, orthosis, walker boot, functional removable immobilisation) after surgical fracture fixation
control_label: Non-removable ankle support (plaster or synthetic cast, non-removable immobilisation) after surgical fracture fixation
outcome_description: Activity limitation / ankle function at end of the treatment (immobilisation) period, measured with patient-reported or clinician-rated ankle function instruments such as the Olerud-Molander Ankle Score (OMAS), Mazur/AOFAS ankle score, Foot and Ankle Outcome Score, Foot and Ankle Ability Measure, Baird-Jackson score, or similar activity/function scales. All instruments are oriented so that higher = better function before pooling as a standardized mean difference.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g means the removable ankle support group had better activity/function (less activity limitation) at end of treatment than the non-removable (cast) group.
search_queries: removable brace versus cast ankle fracture surgery randomized trial functional outcome
postoperative immobilisation orthosis versus plaster cast ankle fracture fixation Olerud-Molander
early functional support versus cast after ankle fracture internal fixation controlled trial outcome
inclusion_criteria: Studies of adults or adolescents who received surgical fixation of an ankle or related lower-limb fracture and then some form of postoperative immobilisation
Compares a removable form of ankle support/immobilisation with a non-removable support such as a cast (any controlled or comparative design, randomised or not)
Reports any quantitative measure of activity limitation, ankle function, or related functional outcome from which an effect size can be derived
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, opinion, commentary, protocol, or purely theoretical/biomechanical modelling paper)
No comparison between a removable support condition and a non-removable/cast control condition (single-arm or before-after only)
No usable quantitative outcome data for computing an effect size (no means with SDs/SEs/CIs, t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios)
Completely unrelated to postoperative ankle/lower-limb fracture immobilisation and functional outcome
moderators_to_extract: Type of removable device (brace, orthosis, walker boot, functional bandage)
Duration of immobilisation and whether early weight-bearing/mobilisation was permitted
Sample size category and risk-of-bias rating
effect_size_note: Pool as standardized mean difference (Hedges g) because studies use different functional instruments (OMAS, Mazur, etc.). Scores are oriented so higher = better function; any instrument where higher = worse must be sign-reversed before pooling. Use end-of-treatment (end of immobilisation period) values; where only change scores or medians/IQRs are reported, convert using standard approximations.
